name: an encrypted vault with a key, in a repository that has the guard

existing.gitattributes:
# Fjord: never diff or merge ciphertext
*.age binary -diff -merge

files.contents:
# age recipients for the Private vault.
#
# One public key per line. Every file in this vault is encrypted to ALL of
# these keys, so any one of them can decrypt it. Add a line per device.
#
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored, so this file is also a
# valid argument to `age -R recipients.txt`.
#
# Add your first key with:
#
#     age-keygen -o ~/.config/fjord/identity.txt
#     age-keygen -y ~/.config/fjord/identity.txt >> Private/recipients.txt
#
# Until at least one key is present, nothing can be written to this vault.
#
# Removing a key here stops FUTURE files being encrypted to it. It does not
# revoke anything: every version already in git history stays readable by
# that key forever. See "Rotating and revoking keys" in the root README.

age1ql3z7hjy54pw3hyww5ayyfg7zqgvc7w3j2elw8zmrj2kg5sfn9aqmcac8p

# Plaintext guard for an encrypted vault.
#
# Ignore everything, then allow back only the things that belong in an
# encrypted vault. This is what stops a decrypted working copy — say you ran
# `age -d` to edit a file in another editor and forgot to clean up — from
# being committed in the clear.
#
# Do not remove these lines. If you add a new allowed file type to this
# vault, add a matching `!` rule rather than deleting the `*`.

*

# Let git descend into subdirectories.
!*/

# Encrypted payloads.
!*.age

# Vault machinery (must stay readable to find the keys and the format).
!fjord.vault.json
!recipients.txt
!.gitignore
